hierarchy.label: DBMS UNIT - I: Database System Concepts, ER Model & Relational Design

children.label: 1. Database Fundamentals & Engine Architecture
Database Systems vs. File Systems
Enterprise Applications Domain
Mission-Critical Systems (Banking transactions, Airline reservations & Telecommunication billing)
Enterprise Operations (University student records, Financial accounting & Human Resource payroll)
File System Critical Drawbacks
Data Redundancy & Inconsistency (Duplicate data across multiple files causing wasted storage and desynchronization)
Difficulty Accessing Data (Need to write new specialized programs for every ad-hoc request)
Data Isolation & Integrity Problems (Data scattered in diverse formats + Inflexible hardcoded integrity constraints)
Atomicity, Concurrency & Security Flaws (Inconsistent states on power crashes, race condition anomalies & coarse-grained security)
Data Abstraction & Three-Schema Architecture
Three Levels of Data Abstraction
Physical Level (Lowest level describing complex low-level data structures and record layouts on storage media)
Logical Level (Middle level describing what data is stored and structural relationships among all entities)
View Level (Highest level describing customized subsets of the database tailored to specific user personas)
Dual Data Independence Principles
Physical Data Independence (Capacity to modify physical storage schemas or indexes without altering logical schemas)
Logical Data Independence (Capacity to modify logical schemas without altering external views or application programs)
Database Instances vs. Schemas
Database Schema (Overall static skeleton design and type definitions analogous to variable declarations in programming)
Database Instance (Dynamic snapshot collection of information stored in the database at a specific moment in time)
Data Models & Database Languages
Four Primary Data Model Paradigms
Relational Model (Collection of tables with rows and columns representing data records and relations)
Entity-Relationship Model (Collection of basic objects called entities and relationship sets for conceptual design)
Object-Based Models (Object-oriented and object-relational encapsulating methods, identity, and complex data structures)
Semi-Structured Data Model (Data specifications allowing individual data items of same type to have different attribute sets e.g. XML & JSON)
DDL vs. DML Languages
Data-Definition Language / DDL (Specifies database schema structure, produces system catalog metadata, and enforces integrity constraints)
Procedural DML (Requires user to specify what data is needed and how to retrieve those data step-by-step)
Declarative / Non-Procedural DML (Requires user to specify what data is needed without specifying how to retrieve it e.g. SQL)
Application Program Access Methods
Embedded SQL (Host language pre-processor converting EXEC SQL statements into procedural runtime API calls)
Application Program Interfaces (Dynamic SQL execution libraries such as ODBC for C/C++ and JDBC for Java)
DBMS Engine Internals & System Structure
Transaction Management & ACID Rules
Transaction Definition (A collection of operations that performs a single logical function in a database application)
ACID Invariants (Atomicity all-or-nothing, Consistency preserving invariants, Isolation concurrency protection, Durability persistent commits)
Core Transaction Modules (Concurrency Control Manager coordinating concurrent execution + Recovery Manager ensuring state restoration)
Query Processing Engine Components
DDL Interpreter (Parses and executes DDL schema statements, recording definitions in data dictionary metadata)
DML Compiler & Optimizer (Parses DML queries, translates into relational algebra expressions, and selects lowest-cost execution plan)
Query Evaluation Engine (Executes low-level primitive physical instructions generated by query optimizer)
Storage Manager Modules & Data Structures
Storage Control Modules (Authorization & Integrity Manager, Transaction Manager, File Manager & Buffer Manager caching blocks)
Physical Disk Data Structures (Data Files storing records, Data Dictionary storing schema metadata & Indices providing rapid lookup)
System Architecture, User Personas & History
Two-Tier vs. Three-Tier Client-Server Architecture
Two-Tier Architecture (Client machine runs user interface and business logic, invoking SQL on database system directly via ODBC/JDBC)
Three-Tier Architecture (Client web browser interfaces with Application Server business logic, which in turn coordinates with Database Server)
User Hierarchy & DBA Responsibilities
Four Database User Classes (Naive users via forms, Application programmers writing software, Sophisticated analysts & Specialized engineers)
Database Administrator / DBA Mandate (Schema definition, Storage structure & access method selection, User privilege authorization & Periodic backups)
Historical Evolution Milestones
Early Eras (1950s-1960s magnetic tapes & file systems; CODASYL network model and IBM IMS hierarchical database)
Relational Revolution (1970 Edgar F. Codd relational model paper; IBM System R and UC Berkeley Ingres prototypes)
Modern Eras (1980s ANSI SQL standardization; 1990s Data Warehousing & Object-Relational; 2000s Web XML & Cloud Big Data)
2. Conceptual Database Design & ER Modeling
Database Design Lifecycle Phases
Phase 1 - Requirements Analysis
User Requirement Gathering (Interviews and documentation reviews with prospective database users)
Operational Specification (Identifying functional business workflows and expected query/transaction workloads)
Phase 2 & 3 - Conceptual & Logical Design
Conceptual Database Design (Developing a high-level enterprise ER schema independent of DBMS implementation)
Logical Database Design (Mapping conceptual ER schema into target DBMS data model e.g. Relational tables)
Phase 4, 5 & 6 - Refinement, Physical & Security
Schema Refinement (Analyzing relational schemas using Normalization theory to eliminate update redundancies and anomalies)
Physical Design & Tuning (Selecting file organizations, clustering, primary/secondary indexes, and buffer parameters)
Security Design (Specifying user roles, discretionary access controls, and view-level authorization masks)
ER Diagram Standard Geometric Notations
Primary Structural Shapes
Rectangles (Entity sets) & Double Rectangles (Weak entity sets dependent on identifying owner)
Diamonds (Relationship sets) & Double Diamonds (Identifying relationship sets for weak entities)
Connecting Lines (Links attributes to entity sets and entity sets to relationship sets)
Attribute & Constraint Geometric Styles
Ellipses (Standard attributes) & Underlined Ellipse Text (Primary key attribute identifiers)
Double Ellipses (Multivalued attributes) & Dashed Ellipses (Derived attributes computed dynamically)
Dashed Underline Text (Discriminator / Partial key attribute of weak entity set)
Double Lines (Total participation / existence dependency) & Directed Arrows (Key constraints)
Entity Concepts & Attribute Typologies
Entity & Entity Set Definitions
Entity Definition (A real-world object that is distinguishable from all other objects e.g. specific employee)
Entity Set Definition (A collection of similar entities of the same type that share identical attribute properties)
Strong vs. Weak Entities (Strong entities possess independent key attributes; Weak entities require owner key)
Attribute Dimension Matrix
Simple / Atomic vs. Composite Attributes (Indivisible units vs Hierarchical components e.g. Name decomposed into First, Middle, Last)
Single-Valued vs. Multivalued Attributes (Single scalar value e.g. SSN or DOB vs Set of multiple values e.g. phone_numbers or degrees)
Stored vs. Derived Attributes (Physically stored in database vs Dynamically computed on-the-fly e.g. Age computed from DOB and Current_Date)
Null Value Semantics (Represents missing values, unknown values, or inapplicable attribute contexts)
Relationships & Mapping Cardinality Constraints
Relationship Set & Degree Dimensions
Relationship Set (A mathematical relation on n >= 2 entity sets, representing associations among entities e.g. Works_In or Enrolls)
Degree of Relationship (Number of participating entity sets: Binary = 2 sets, Ternary = 3 sets, n-ary = general)
Descriptive Attributes (Attributes belonging to relationship set itself rather than participating entities e.g. since or hours)
Four Mapping Cardinalities
One-to-One / 1:1 Cardinality (An entity in A is associated with at most one entity in B, and B with at most one in A)
One-to-Many / 1:N Cardinality (An entity in A is associated with any number in B, while an entity in B is associated with at most one in A)
Many-to-One / N:1 Cardinality (Entities in A are associated with at most one in B, while an entity in B is associated with any number in A)
Many-to-Many / M:N Cardinality (An entity in A is associated with any number in B, and an entity in B is associated with any number in A)
Key Constraints on Relationships
Directed Arrow Representation (Arrow from relationship pointing to entity set indicates at most one relationship instance per entity)
Department Manages Example (Arrow towards Departments in Manages indicates each department has at most one manager)
Strict 1:1 Arrow Rule (Arrows pointing to both entity sets enforce strict one-to-one mapping across both domains)
3. Advanced ER & Extended ER (EER) Mechanisms
Participation Constraints & Existence Dependency
Total Participation Semantics
Double-Line Representation (Signifies that every entity in the entity set must participate in at least one relationship instance)
Existence Dependency (Entities cannot exist in the database without an associated relationship instance e.g. every Department must have a Manager)
Partial Participation Semantics
Single-Line Representation (Signifies that entities in the entity set can optionally participate in relationship instances)
Selective Association (e.g. only a small subset of Employees participate as managers in the Manages relationship set)
Weak Entity Sets & Identifying Relationships
Structural Anatomy of Weak Entity Sets
Identifying Owner Entity Set (Strong entity set providing primary key context for weak entity existence)
Identifying Relationship Set (Represented by double diamond, linking weak entity to owner with mandatory total participation)
Partial Key / Discriminator (Underlined with dashed line, uniquely distinguishes weak entities associated with same owner)
Formulation & Academic Examples
Primary Key Synthesis Rule (Primary Key = Owner Entity Primary Key + Weak Entity Partial Key / Discriminator)
Dependents of Employees (Dependents weak entity identified by pname discriminator combined with Employee ssn)
Course Offerings of University (Course_Offering weak entity identified by sec_no and semester combined with Course_No)
Class Hierarchies & ISA Abstractions
Specialization vs. Generalization
Generalization (Bottom-up design process synthesizing common attributes of lower-level entity sets into a higher-level superclass)
Specialization (Top-down design process decomposing a higher-level entity set into specialized sub-groups based on distinct roles)
Attribute Inheritance (Subclasses automatically inherit all attributes and relationship memberships of their superclass)
Hierarchy Constraint Dimensions
Overlap Constraints (Overlapping allows an entity instance to belong to multiple subclasses vs Disjoint enforcing mutual exclusivity)
Covering / Completeness Constraints (Total Covering requires every superclass entity to be in at least one subclass vs Partial Covering)
Aggregation & Enterprise Conceptual Design
Aggregation Modeling Pattern
Aggregation Construct (Encapsulates a relationship set and participating entities as a higher-level abstract entity)
Overcoming ER Relationship Boundaries (Allows associating a relationship set with another relationship set e.g. Sponsors relationship linking to Projects-Monitors)
Aggregation vs. Ternary Relationship (Aggregation preserves independent binary relationship semantics and permits distinct key constraints)
Enterprise Design Decision Dilemmas
Entity vs. Attribute Choice (Use entity if object has internal attributes or dynamic lifecycle; use attribute if atomic descriptor)
Entity vs. Relationship Choice (Use relationship for pure associations; use entity if association itself has rich attributes or connects other relationships)
Binary vs. Ternary Relationship Selection (Decompose ternary into binary if independent constraints apply; retain ternary if relationship is atomic)
4. Relational Model Foundations & Integrity Constraints
Relational Data Model Structure & Terminology
Core Relational Building Blocks
Relation Schema & Instance (Schema defines relation name, column names and types; Instance is a set of distinct tuples/records)
Tuples & Attributes (Tuple corresponds to a row or record; Attribute corresponds to a column or named field with a defined domain)
Domain / Data Type (Set of permitted atomic scalar values e.g. INTEGER, CHAR(20), REAL)
Mathematical Dimensions of Relations
Relation Degree / Arity (The total number of attributes / columns in the relation schema)
Relation Cardinality (The total number of tuples / rows currently stored in the relation instance)
Integrity Constraints Classification
Domain Constraints & Entity Integrity
Domain Constraint (Every attribute value must be an atomic element drawn from the specified domain)
Entity Integrity Rule (No attribute participating in the primary key of a relation can accept NULL values)
Key Constraints Hierarchy
Super Key (Any subset of attributes that uniquely identifies every tuple within the relation)
Candidate Key (A minimal super key such that no proper subset can uniquely identify tuples)
Primary Key (A designated candidate key chosen by the database designer as the principal tuple identifier)
Foreign Key & General Semantic Constraints
Foreign Key & Referential Integrity (A set of fields in referencing relation referring to primary key of referenced relation)
Referential Integrity Invariant (Foreign key value must match an existing primary key value in referenced relation or be NULL)
General Semantic Constraints (Table CHECK constraints and assertions restricting allowable data states e.g. CHECK (rating BETWEEN 1 AND 10))
Constraint Enforcement & Referential Actions
Violation Triggers on DML Operations
Insert Violations (Can violate domain, entity integrity, primary key uniqueness, or foreign key target validity)
Delete Violations (Can violate referential integrity if a referenced primary key tuple is deleted while referencing foreign keys exist)
Update Violations (Can violate both primary key uniqueness and foreign key referential integrity on either side)
SQL Referential Integrity Actions
NO ACTION / RESTRICT (Default action rejecting the deletion or update of referenced tuple with an error)
CASCADE (Automatically propagates the deletion or update of referenced tuple to all matching referencing tuples)
SET NULL (Sets the foreign key columns of all referencing tuples to NULL when referenced tuple is deleted or updated)
SET DEFAULT (Sets the foreign key columns of all referencing tuples to a specified default value upon modification)
5. Logical Database Design (ER-to-Relational Translation)
Translating Entity Sets to Relations
Strong Entity Set Mapping Protocol
Direct Column Mapping (Each simple attribute of entity set maps to a column in the newly created table)
Primary Key Preservation (The primary key of the strong entity set directly becomes the PRIMARY KEY of the relation)
Complex Attribute Decompositions
Composite Attribute Flattening (Flattened into individual atomic component columns e.g. Address -> Street, City, State, Zip)
Multivalued Attribute Extraction (Extracted into a separate relation containing owner primary key + attribute value as composite key)
Translating Relationship Sets to Relations
Many-to-Many / M:N Relationship Translation
Junction Relation Creation (Creates a dedicated relation containing foreign keys referencing both participating entity tables)
Composite Primary Key Formation (The primary key of the junction table is the composite union of both entity primary keys)
Descriptive Attribute Retention (Any descriptive attributes of the relationship set become columns in the junction table)
Key Constraints & Relation Folding (1:N and 1:1)
Option 1 - Dedicated Relation (Create separate table where primary key is strictly the primary key of the entity on the constrained side)
Option 2 - Relation Folding / Combination (Fold relationship attributes and foreign key directly into the relation of the entity on the many side e.g. Dept_Mgr)
Enforcing Participation Constraints in SQL
NOT NULL Constraint Enforcement (In folded table, declare foreign key as NOT NULL to enforce total participation e.g. mgr_ssn in Departments)
Combining 1:1 Total Relations (When both sides have total participation, combine both entities and relationship into a single unified table)
Translating Weak Entity Sets
Relational Formulation of Weak Entities
Composite Primary Key Structure (Primary key consists of Owner Entity Primary Key + Weak Entity Partial Key / Discriminator)
Foreign Key with ON DELETE CASCADE (Foreign key references owner relation with mandatory ON DELETE CASCADE clause)
Identifying Relationship Subsumption (Identifying relationship set is eliminated as a separate table and folded into weak entity relation)
SQL DDL Implementation Example
Dependents Schema (CREATE TABLE Dependents (pname CHAR(20), ssn CHAR(11), cost REAL, PRIMARY KEY (pname, ssn), FOREIGN KEY (ssn) REFERENCES Employees ON DELETE CASCADE))
Cascading Lifecycle Guarantee (Deleting an employee record automatically triggers immediate cascading purge of all corresponding dependent tuples)
Translating ISA Class Hierarchies & Aggregations
General 3-Table ISA Mapping Approach
Superclass Base Table (Creates relation for superclass storing primary key and all common shared attributes)
Subclass Specialized Tables (Creates relations for subclasses storing primary key and specific attributes, where primary key is foreign key to superclass)
Universal Constraint Support (Works flawlessly across all combinations of overlap and covering constraints)
Alternative 2-Table ISA Mapping Approach
Subclass-Only Relations (Creates relations only for subclasses, copying all superclass attributes into each subclass table)
Prerequisite Condition (Only valid when specialization is strictly Disjoint and Total/Covering; duplicate superclass updates are avoided)
Translating Aggregations & Binary Decompositions
Aggregation Relational Translation (Creates table for aggregated relationship, and higher-level relationship contains foreign key to it)
Binary vs. Ternary Decomposition in SQL (Binary decomposition uses separate relations e.g. Policies and Dependents with specific foreign keys, avoiding ternary null anomalies)
6. Relational Querying, Views & Schema Evolution
Relational Querying Principles
Declarative SQL Query Paradigm
Query Definition & Result (A question about the data resulting in a newly computed relation containing matching answer tuples)
Core Relational Operators (SELECT projection choosing columns, WHERE restriction filtering rows, FROM join combining relations)
Academic Query Examples
Projection & Restriction Queries (e.g. SELECT sname, gpa FROM Students WHERE gpa > 3.0)
Multi-Table Relational Joins (e.g. SELECT S.sname, E.cid FROM Students S, Enrolled E WHERE S.sid = E.sid AND E.grade = 'A')
Relational Views Architecture & Applications
View Definition & Virtual Semantics
Virtual Table Concept (A relation that is not part of the conceptual physical model but is made visible to users as a virtual relation)
SQL View Definition Syntax (CREATE VIEW view_name AS SELECT query_expression; stored as query definition in data dictionary)
Dynamic Query Re-evaluation (Standard views are computed on-the-fly dynamically whenever referenced in queries)
Core Architectural View Benefits
Logical Data Independence (Shields user applications from disruptions when base relation schemas are restructured)
Security & Fine-Grained Access Control (Hides sensitive attributes and rows from unauthorized users without multiple base copies)
Query Simplification (Encapsulates frequently-used complex multi-table joins into clean virtual relations)
Materialized Views Mechanism
Physical Result Caching (Precomputes and physically persists the view result on disk for high-performance decision support)
View Maintenance Overhead (Requires systematic maintenance protocols: Periodic batch refresh vs Incremental immediate refresh on base table updates)
DDL Schema Evolution & Object Destruction
Destroying Database Objects
DROP TABLE Semantics (Deletes all rows and purges table definition; RESTRICT blocks if foreign keys exist, CASCADE automatically purges referencing objects)
DROP VIEW Semantics (Deletes view query definition from system catalog without deleting or altering underlying base table data)
Modifying Relational Table Schemas
ALTER TABLE ADD Column (Adds a new column definition to existing table; existing tuples receive NULL or defined DEFAULT value)
ALTER TABLE DROP Column (Deletes an existing column from table schema and removes attribute data across all tuples)
